frozen_decisions_applied: Plan S5 #14: 'Redact all key/credential material from logs, crash reports and completion evidence.' -- addressed as three distinct, concretely grounded pieces of work rather than one generic mechanism, matching the plan's own three-way split: (1) a length-only, content-blind logging redaction utility wired into secure_storage_port.cpp's newly-added diagnostic logging; (2) a new forbidden Kconfig symbol (CONFIG_ESP_COREDUMP_CAPTURE_DRAM) in the plan #3 verifier, grounded in real ESP-IDF espcoredump Kconfig source; (3) a direct grep audit of this repository's own implementation-evidence/*.json and docs/security/*.md files for leaked secret material.

This project's established real-tool-grounding discipline was applied to the crash-report clause exactly as to every other new Kconfig/API reference in S5: CONFIG_ESP_COREDUMP_CAPTURE_DRAM's existence, help text and default value were confirmed by grepping components/espcoredump/Kconfig inside espressif/idf:release-v5.5 before adding it anywhere.

The redaction utility deliberately keeps only a byte length, not a content-derived digest -- a stronger, simpler form than scripts/efuse_provisioning_template.py's SHA-256-based redact_key_material() (plan #5/#8), which needs a digest for a real, narrow cross-record-correlation purpose a log line does not have.

logs_clause.detail: secure_log_redaction.hpp/.cpp: redact_value_for_log() reads only value_len, never dereferences value's content (a null value pointer is treated as zero-length regardless of the len argument passed alongside it, so a stale/wrong length can never produce a misleading nonzero summary). format_redacted_value_summary() renders a fixed '[REDACTED N bytes]' string. Wired into secure_storage_port.cpp (previously zero logging across Sections 2.8-2.10): every get/set/erase now logs key name + outcome, and every successful write additionally logs a redacted value summary, all ESP_PLATFORM-only via new SS_LOGI/SS_LOGW macros (no-op on host, matching connectivity_manager.cpp's established CM_LOGI pattern) tagged with a new LOG_TAG_SECURE_STORAGE. Audited every pre-existing ESP_LOG* call in every S5-touched file (hal_nvs.c's 18 statements, predating this sub-slice) and confirmed none prints a raw value -- only key names, lengths and esp_err_to_name() strings; a real, executed check, not an assumption.

crash_reports_clause.detail: Grepped ESP-IDF's real components/espcoredump/Kconfig inside espressif/idf:release-v5.5: CONFIG_ESP_COREDUMP_CAPTURE_DRAM's help text reads 'Include whole .bss and .data sections and heap data into core dump file' -- exactly where secret-namespace values live at runtime. Added to verify_production_security_profile.py's FORBIDDEN_SYMBOLS. Confirmed via the same Kconfig grep that ESP-IDF's own default is fully disabled (ESP_COREDUMP_TO_FLASH_OR_UART defaults to ESP_COREDUMP_ENABLE_TO_NONE), and confirmed via grep across sdkconfig.defaults/sdkconfig.defaults.esp32c6/sdkconfig.production.esp32c6 that none of them touch any coredump symbol -- so no crash report is generated by any build this repository currently produces; this check guards against a future accidental opt-in, not a currently-active leak. Named directly, not hidden: a 'coredump' partition already exists in partitions.csv/partitions.production.csv (0x534000, 64KB, predating S5), suggesting coredump-to-flash was intended for later use -- whether/when to enable it is a separate, unrelated product decision this sub-slice does not make.

completion_evidence_clause.detail: Directly grep-audited this repository's own implementation-evidence/*.json and docs/security/*.md files: searched for PEM markers (BEGIN CERTIFICATE/PRIVATE KEY/RSA/EC PRIVATE), password-shaped key=value patterns, and the specific synthetic test values used throughout this stage's own test files (hunter2, MyNetwork). All three searches returned zero matches -- a real, executed check with a genuinely clean result, consistent with every S5 test file (Sections 2.7-2.11) having used only synthetic placeholder byte patterns from the start.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: The crash-reports clause is addressed by forbidding a specific Kconfig symbol (CONFIG_ESP_COREDUMP_CAPTURE_DRAM) rather than by any code change, since coredump generation itself is not currently enabled anywhere in this repository's sdkconfig.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: There is nothing to redact in a crash report that is never generated; the concrete, grounded action available now is preventing a future misconfiguration from defeating this stage's own redaction intent once/if coredump is ever enabled.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: If a future sub-slice enables coredump-to-flash (the reserved partition suggests this was anticipated), CONFIG_ESP_COREDUMP_CAPTURE_DRAM staying unset (the default) is the only thing currently preventing DRAM/heap contents -- including secret values -- from being captured; this sub-slice does not otherwise verify what a real coredump would or would not contain, since none is ever produced by the current profile.
